liveApiSnapshot.description: The Upshift USDC vault earns yield by lending USDC OTC to overcollateralized institutional borrowers on August. Any deposits not lent out are allocated to top-performing vaults on blue-chip protocols such as Morpho, Euler and Pendle to earn additional APY. Yield for this vault is typically realized across 30 days, depending on when borrowers repay interest rates. It is recommended that users remain deposited for at least 30 days in order to capture all the yield from that month’s loans.

previewDeposit(uint256).details: Allows an on-chain or off-chain user to simulate the effects of their deposit at the current block, given current on-chain conditions. - MUST return as close to and no more than the exact amount of Vault shares that would be minted in a deposit   call in the same transaction. I.e. deposit should return the same or more shares as previewDeposit if called   in the same transaction. - MUST NOT account for deposit limits like those returned from maxDeposit and should always act as though the   deposit would be accepted, regardless if the user has enough tokens approved, etc. - MUST be inclusive of deposit fees. Integrators should be aware of the existence of deposit fees. - MUST NOT revert. NOTE: any unfavorable discrepancy between convertToShares and previewDeposit SHOULD be considered slippage in share price or some other type of condition, meaning the depositor will lose assets by depositing.

previewMint(uint256).details: Allows an on-chain or off-chain user to simulate the effects of their mint at the current block, given current on-chain conditions. - MUST return as close to and no fewer than the exact amount of assets that would be deposited in a mint call   in the same transaction. I.e. mint should return the same or fewer assets as previewMint if called in the   same transaction. - MUST NOT account for mint limits like those returned from maxMint and should always act as though the mint   would be accepted, regardless if the user has enough tokens approved, etc. - MUST be inclusive of deposit fees. Integrators should be aware of the existence of deposit fees. - MUST NOT revert. NOTE: any unfavorable discrepancy between convertToAssets and previewMint SHOULD be considered slippage in share price or some other type of condition, meaning the depositor will lose assets by minting.

previewRedeem(uint256).details: Allows an on-chain or off-chain user to simulate the effects of their redeemption at the current block, given current on-chain conditions. - MUST return as close to and no more than the exact amount of assets that would be withdrawn in a redeem call   in the same transaction. previewWithdraw(uint256).details: Allows an on-chain or off-chain user to simulate the effects of their withdrawal at the current block, given current on-chain conditions. - MUST return as close to and no fewer than the exact amount of Vault shares that would be burned in a withdraw   call in the same transaction. devdoc.details: This contract implements a proxy that is upgradeable by an admin. To avoid https://medium.com/nomic-labs-blog/malicious-backdoors-in-ethereum-proxies-62629adf3357[proxy selector clashing], which can potentially be used in an attack, this contract uses the https://blog.openzeppelin.com/the-transparent-proxy-pattern/[transparent proxy pattern]. This pattern implies two things that go hand in hand: 1. If any account other than the admin calls the proxy, the call will be forwarded to the implementation, even if that call matches one of the admin functions exposed by the proxy itself. 2. warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI inventory only, not proof of current runtime bytecode identity, execution success, funding, liquidity, complete workflows or financial safety. Zero native value is required; independent grants, pauses, canonical-calldata and safety controls remain authoritative.

This is Upshift own Ethereum upUSDC lending pool, not a second AugustVaults protocol and not a curator wrapper over an already admitted protocol. Current official API identifies chain 1, Upshift USDC, status active and withdrawal_only=false. Older initial implementation 0x43D41393124Dfca45567Ef005F5C79311C57c65b from deployment docs is not the reported current LendingPoolv3 implementation 0xc0026E559dA7F2d4eE573616C09A8F721fa599bd; source-service runtime/creation status for that implementation is match, not exact_match.

Underlying is Ethereum USDC 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 with 6 decimals; upUSDC shares also have 6 decimals in the explorer snapshot. deposit spends exact USDC base units via caller allowance to this pool and rounds shares down, rejecting zero shares. mint specifies share base units, rounds required assets up and uses caller USDC allowance. Supply and per-deposit caps, receiver validity, configured asset and blacklists apply. Neither entry has a caller-set minimum shares, maximum assets or deadline.

requestRedeem takes share base units from holderAddr into pool custody rather than burning immediately; a different caller needs existing holder share allowance. It computes floor-rounded underlying, subtracts floor withdrawalFee*basis/10000, rejects zero proceeds and fixes receiver/date claim accounting. No standalone prefunding or admin loan funding is admitted. With lagDuration=0 the request immediately calls _claim and burns the escrowed shares; otherwise the receiver/date is claimable at the UTC processing hour on the date of block.timestamp+5 minutes+lagDuration. This is not a guaranteed exact-duration delay.

Anyone may call claim for a recorded receiver and date, but funds always go to that receiver; returns are (sharesBurned, assetsTransferred), despite generic docs describing a different order. Shares burn only when claim settles. Configured withdrawal pause and caller/holder/receiver blacklists can revert ordinary exits; insufficient pool-held USDC reverts payment. Batch settlement, privileged loans and collateral/liquidation management are excluded. ERC4626 withdraw/redeem unconditionally revert WithdrawalRequestRequired and are excluded; instantRedeem described by the generic interface is absent from this deployed ABI.

Explorer point-in-time fields show depositsPaused=false, withdrawalsPaused=false, lagDuration=0, liquidationHour=0, managementFeePercent=0, withdrawalFee=0. These are not persistent state guarantees. Owner can change fees, blacklist accounts, pause entries/exits, manage loans and upgrade the proxy; timelock duration changes consume a configured scheduler call. Management fees reduce asset accounting when charged; totalAssets includes loan principal plus pool USDC minus accrued fees, not only immediately available cash.

Official docs permit partner-specific KYC and wallet screening. Reviewed direct entry bodies enforce blacklisting, not an affirmative KYC allowlist; this does not establish user legal eligibility or permission to use institutional features. No APR, collateral adequacy or loan repayment assertion is made.

Older initial implementation 0x43D41393124Dfca45567Ef005F5C79311C57c65b from deployment docs is not the reported current LendingPoolv3 implementation 0xc0026E559dA7F2d4eE573616C09A8F721fa599bd; source-service runtime/creation status for that implementation is match, not exact_match.

Underlying is Ethereum USDC 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 with 6 decimals; upUSDC shares also have 6 decimals in the explorer snapshot. deposit spends exact USDC base units via caller allowance to this pool and rounds shares down, rejecting zero shares. mint specifies share base units, rounds required assets up and uses caller USDC allowance. Supply and per-deposit caps, receiver validity, configured asset and blacklists apply. Neither entry has a caller-set minimum shares, maximum assets or deadline.

requestRedeem takes share base units from holderAddr into pool custody rather than burning immediately; a different caller needs existing holder share allowance. It computes floor-rounded underlying, subtracts floor withdrawalFee*basis/10000, rejects zero proceeds and fixes receiver/date claim accounting. No standalone prefunding or admin loan funding is admitted. With lagDuration=0 the request immediately calls _claim and burns the escrowed shares; otherwise the receiver/date is claimable at the UTC processing hour on the date of block.timestamp+5 minutes+lagDuration. This is not a guaranteed exact-duration delay.

Anyone may call claim for a recorded receiver and date, but funds always go to that receiver; returns are (sharesBurned, assetsTransferred), despite generic docs describing a different order. Shares burn only when claim settles. Configured withdrawal pause and caller/holder/receiver blacklists can revert ordinary exits; insufficient pool-held USDC reverts payment. Batch settlement, privileged loans and collateral/liquidation management are excluded. ERC4626 withdraw/redeem unconditionally revert WithdrawalRequestRequired and are excluded; instantRedeem described by the generic interface is absent from this deployed ABI.

Explorer point-in-time fields show depositsPaused=false, withdrawalsPaused=false, lagDuration=0, liquidationHour=0, managementFeePercent=0, withdrawalFee=0. These are not persistent state guarantees. Owner can change fees, blacklist accounts, pause entries/exits, manage loans and upgrade the proxy; timelock duration changes consume a configured scheduler call. Management fees reduce asset accounting when charged; totalAssets includes loan principal plus pool USDC minus accrued fees, not only immediately available cash.

Official docs permit partner-specific KYC and wallet screening. Reviewed direct entry bodies enforce blacklisting, not an affirmative KYC allowlist; this does not establish user legal eligibility or permission to use institutional features. No APR, collateral adequacy or loan repayment assertion is made.
